questions.question: A product title must support full-text search, phrase matching, alphabetical sorting, and display in results. Which field design covers all four behaviors?
options: StoredField only
StringField only
TextField with storage plus a normalized SortedDocValuesField
TextField without storage
questions.explanation: TextField creates the analyzed postings and positions, storage returns the original title, and sorted doc values provide a per-document ordering value.

questions.question: Why should an application-generated SKU usually use TermQuery rather than passing the SKU through QueryParser?
options: QueryParser cannot create any TermQuery objects
The application already owns the exact structured value and should preserve the same normalization used by StringField
TermQuery automatically sorts every result
QueryParser only works with numeric fields
questions.explanation: Lucene's parser guidance distinguishes human-entered text from program-generated values. Exact identifiers should be constructed directly and consistently.

questions.question: What must be indexed for PhraseQuery to verify term order?
options: Only stored fields
Term positions in the postings representation
Only sorted doc values
A commit user-data map
questions.explanation: Phrase matching uses indexed term positions. A stored value can be returned, but it is not the search structure used to verify phrase order.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates near-real-time visibility from durability?
options: Every flush is an fsynced commit
A refreshed reader can expose changes from an IndexWriter before a durable commit, while commit syncs referenced files for crash survival
Segment merges are the only way readers see new documents
Stored fields become durable without IndexWriter
questions.explanation: Lucene can open or refresh near-real-time readers from an IndexWriter. IndexWriter.commit is the separate operation that syncs a commit point and its files.

questions.question: A price is indexed as IntField. Which query best expresses the application-owned range 1000-2500 cents?
options: A WildcardQuery over the decimal string
A PhraseQuery with both bounds
IntField.newRangeQuery with validated integer bounds
A QueryParser expression over a StoredField
questions.explanation: The typed range API matches the typed field representation and avoids converting numeric application data into text syntax.

questions.question: What is the safest way to tune Lucene latency or throughput for a production workload?
options: Use a universal formula based only on document count
Force-merge after every write
Benchmark representative documents and queries while observing refresh, segment, merge, cache, storage, and tail-latency behavior
Increase every buffer and clause limit
questions.explanation: Lucene performance depends on field design, analyzers, query shapes, hardware, concurrency, refresh policy, segments, and merges. Representative measurement is the defensible basis for tuning.
